source_secondary: World Bank Open Data API (FX.OWN.TOTL.ZS, mobileaccount.t.d, account.t.d, fin2.t.d, FX.OWN.TOTL.SO.ZS)
World Bank Findex Chapter 1 / Chapter 2 narrative briefs
notes_general: Vietnam (VN) was not part of the Findex 2021 wave (added in Findex 2022 / 2025); we backfill with the 2022 datapoint where available and mark imputed. Brunei (BN) is not in Findex at all (high-income, never surveyed); flagged null. 'mobile_money_pct' here uses the Findex indicator 'mobile money account (% age 15+)' which in upper-middle/high-income ASEAN often captures GrabPay/TrueMoney/GCash/Touch'n Go-type e-wallets (per Findex 2021 methodology, mobile money = mobile-money-service provider, broad).

VN.notes: Vietnam was NOT surveyed in Findex 2021 wave. Values shown are Findex 2022 (account ownership 56.27%, mobile money 16.47%) from World Bank API (FX.OWN.TOTL.ZS, mobileaccount.t.d). 2017 baseline was 30.8% account / 3.5% mobile money. bank_account / digital_payment 2021-equivalent not directly available.

ID.notes: account_pct from World Bank API FX.OWN.TOTL.ZS (Findex 2021). mobile_money_pct from mobileaccount.t.d. bank_account_pct estimated from Indonesia financial institution account (account-mobile, approx). digital_payment_pct estimated best-effort from Findex 2021 country brief / Bank Indonesia citations; note 75M Indonesians paid via mobile (~37% of 15+ pop).

PH.notes: From Findex 2021 (account 51.4%, financial institution 46.0%, mobile money 21.7%). digital_payment_pct ~42.5% per Findex 2021 chapter 2 / PIDS citations. Source: Bangko Sentral / Findex country profile.

TH.notes: account_pct from FX.OWN.TOTL.ZS Findex 2021. mobile_money_pct 60.0% from mobileaccount.t.d (this captures PromptPay + TrueMoney + e-wallets per WB definition). digital_payment_pct 92.0% widely cited from Findex 2021 (BOT/Thai academic references). Bank account approximated from financial institution account (~95%).

MY.notes: account_pct from FX.OWN.TOTL.ZS Findex 2021. mobile_money_pct from mobileaccount.t.d (Touch'n Go, GrabPay, Boost). bank_account_pct estimated ~87.5% (account minus mobile-only). digital_payment_pct ~79% best-effort from Findex 2021 narrative.

SG.notes: account_pct 97.55% from FX.OWN.TOTL.ZS Findex 2021. mobile_money_pct 30.6% from mobileaccount.t.d (PayNow / GrabPay). digital_payment_pct ~96% best-effort high-income ASEAN benchmark (Findex 2021 high-income avg digital pay 95%+).

KH.notes: account_pct 33.39% from Findex 2021 (FX.OWN.TOTL.ZS). mobile_money_pct 6.60% from mobileaccount.t.d. Note: NBC Bakong shifts likely captured in 2022+ data, not 2021. digital_payment best-effort.

LA.notes: account_pct 37.32% from Findex 2021. mobile_money_pct 5.48%. bank_account / digital_payment best-effort from Findex chapter narrative.

MM.notes: account_pct 47.79% from Findex 2021 (jumped from 26% in 2017). mobile_money_pct ~29% (Wave Money, KBZPay surge). NOTE: in Myanmar mobile_money_pct > bank_account_pct → strong leapfrog. digital_payment best-effort.

BN.notes: Brunei Darussalam is NOT covered by the World Bank Findex Database (high-income, small population, never surveyed in 2014/2017/2021/2025 waves). For ASEAN10 analysis, use Autoriti Monetari Brunei Darussalam (AMBD) reports as proxy: AMBD 2021 estimates ~99% bank account ownership, ~70%+ digital payment usage. No comparable Findex figure exists.

leapfrog_index.definition: leapfrog = max(0, mobile_money_pct - bank_account_pct) / account_pct. Captures degree to which mobile money outpaces conventional banking within the account-owning population.
leapfrog_index.notable: Only Myanmar shows mobile_money > bank_account in Findex 2021 (29% vs 28%). Cambodia and Lao PDR have low mobile money but very low bank account; Vietnam likely shows leapfrog by 2022 wave (16.5% mobile money on a 56% account base, with bank infrastructure lagging in rural areas).
leapfrog_index.caveat: Findex 'mobile money account' in upper-middle-income ASEAN (TH/MY/SG) bundles e-wallets that are bank-linked, so the metric is NOT purely 'unbanked mobile money'. Real leapfrog story is clearest in MM, KH, LA, VN.

hypotheses.title: リープフロッグ強度と政情脆弱性は逆U字
hypotheses.expected: 極端に低い国 (SG/TH) は伝統金融が強く政情も安定。極端に高い国 (MM) は伝統金融が脆弱で政情も脆弱。中間 (PH/ID/KH) は『便利な飛び石』として最も成長余地があるが、ハッキング・詐欺リスクという不可視コストも最大化する仮説。

hypotheses.title: デジタル決済普及率と現金経済の『見えないコスト』随伴
hypotheses.expected: TH (92%)・SG (96%) はデジタル決済が高く、表面の便利さが進む一方で、税務透明性が上がり個人プライバシーが収縮（不可視コスト）。逆にMM/KH (30%前後) は便利さは低いが、現金経済のクッションが残る（不安定だが匿名性のコスト回避）。便利さと監視は随伴する。

hypotheses.title: 口座保有率ギャップ＝モバイル金融の救済容量
hypotheses.expected: account_pct が中位 (KH 33%, LA 37%, MM 48%) の国ほど、追加成長は伝統金融ではなくモバイルから来る。Findex 2025 で確認できる『次の5年』を予言できる仮説。Vietnam は2021データ欠損だが2022時点で account 56% / mobile 16% で代表例。

hypotheses.title: 高デジタル決済国ほど災害・通信断のとき随伴コストが顕在化
hypotheses.expected: PH/ID は災害頻度が高くデジタル決済中位 → 通信断時の経済停止リスクが高い。TH は災害+デジタル超高 → 最も脆弱な組み合わせ。SG は災害ほぼゼロのため随伴コスト無視できる。『便利さ』が同じでも、地震・洪水多発国では不可視コストが膨らむ。

hypotheses.title: モバイル金融急増国は信用市場の不可視リスクが先行する
hypotheses.expected: Myanmar (+~25pt)、Philippines (大幅増)、Indonesia は短期間にモバイル経由マイクロ与信が普及→隠れた家計債務の急増。Findex で『便利』が拡大した国ほど、家計レベルのデジタル過剰借入という不可視コストが2〜3年遅れて表面化する仮説。Khan Bank, GCash, GoTo Financial の与信残高で検証可能。
